intro: 3MF to STL converts 3D models from 3MF to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to use a PrusaSlicer or Bambu Studio project in a printer, slicer or program that only accepts STL. STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours, as text (ASCII) or binary.

3MF is the modern 3D printing format: a ZIP with the model in XML that stores units, several named parts and the colour of each face, opened directly by PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Cura and Windows. Units are read from the 3MF itself; choose the units you want for the STL and the measurements are converted, because STL does not store them and almost every program reads it in millimetres. You can also apply a scale, for example 0.5 to print the 3MF at half size.

STL does not store colours: if the original has them, the result comes out without them and the note says so. If the 3MF has several parts, you can keep them separate inside the STL when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The geometry is not simplified or repaired: every triangle of the 3MF reaches the STL unchanged, with duplicate vertices merged. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, checked before the file is processed. Files are deleted automatically when they expire.
steps: Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.
